book.title: The Book of Joy
book.author: Dalai Lama, Desmond Tutu and Douglas Abrams

confidence_note: Quotes and exile passage verified in the CBS News excerpt. Tutu's remark about being sulky is only in a secondary summary and left out of the story. Old text's invented Tutu-asks scene, apartheid dancing and quotes dropped.
facts: The Dalai Lama: when he looks only at the difficulties in his own country he worries.
When he widens his view to include others' suffering, including Hui Muslims in China, his own suffering lessens.
Abrams: this is a shift from anguish toward compassion, not a denial of pain.
'If I remained in the Potala in Lhasa, I would have stayed in what has often been described as a golden cage.'
'So, personally, I prefer the last five decades of refugee life.'
'Wherever you have friends that's your country, and wherever you receive love, that's your home.'
Abrams links this to the saying 'Pain is inevitable; suffering is optional' and to the Buddhist Sallatha Sutta.
Abrams notes the Dalai Lama sees his situation as connected to other people's, not set against theirs.
scene_details: the Dalai Lama cupping his hands in a small circle and widening them
the golden cage of the Potala
tension: A man who lost his country says he prefers the life of a refugee.
opening_idea: Open on the Dalai Lama's hands, cupped into a small circle and then opened wide.

lessons.idea: Widen the frame around your own trouble.
lessons.anchor: His view of Tibetans and of others' suffering.
lessons.example: After a rejection, look at how many others have faced the same.

reflect_final: What is one difficulty of yours that looks different if you widen the circle to include others who face something similar?

use_cases.situation: A friend is consumed by their own bad news.
use_cases.move: Ask who else they know who is in a similar spot and what that person needs.

use_cases.situation: You are stuck on a problem at work.
use_cases.move: List what you have gained from the situation, as the Dalai Lama does with refugee life.

use_cases.situation: A teammate is bitter after a move.
use_cases.move: Ask what the new place makes possible.

pocket_idea: The Dalai Lama calls the Potala a golden cage; widen your view and a loss can show what it opened.

conversation_variants.punchline_idea: The Dalai Lama says he prefers five decades as a refugee to the Potala.
conversation_variants.thirty_sec_idea: Asked about exile, the Dalai Lama widened his hands to show his view: he worries when he looks only at Tibet, but others suffer too. He called the Potala a golden cage.
